title: Intentional Peer Support:
length: about 2:15 as planned; about 1:35 with every TRIM and the “cut first” row
headline: Men serving long sentences run peer support for each other inside a Nebraska prison. It changed them, and it changed the prison.
story: At RTC in Lincoln (the men still call it LCC), men in prison are trained IPS peer specialists. They talk over cards and chess, the prison now calls them before it uses force, and one of them helps young men earn their diplomas. “It could be the thing that saves your life.”
The men are the voices. MHA staff appear only for one line at the top. Documentary tone, but hopeful: their past is in their own words, then the video moves on with them.

Small name super, 3 s, the first time each man speaks: name · IPS peer specialist.
Keep the use-of-force line whole. It is the proof the culture changed.
Cards and chess → the tables and the handshake. Diploma → his book. Otherwise stay on the speaker.
Lift the dim interview shots gently. Do not crush the blacks.
dont: No crime, sentence or facility name on any super or card. Herman's crime line stays in his own voice only.
No MHA staff as heroes. No fundraising ask.
No sound from C4771 (the “bam, bam, bam” story). Picture only.
No readable ID badge or name tag. No second aspect ratio.
